clue.text: Vicar in wrong circle

indicators.note: something done wrong is muddled, so the letters of circle are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A clergyman has got himself into the wrong social set.
explanation.definitionFit: A vicar is a parish priest, one kind of clergyman in holy orders.

clue.text: One left standing

parts.note: read as a leftist who stands at an election, rather than the last survivor of some contest

explanation.surface: The sole survivor, still on their feet when everyone else has fallen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' is the political left and 'standing' is running for office, so this is a person contesting a seat for Britain's main left-of-centre party.
explanation.definitionFit: A person nominated by the Labour Party to contest an election is standing for that left-wing party.

clue.text: Spacious yacht's first to tie up, heading north

indicators.note: in a down entry, going north means the letters are read from the bottom up
the first letter of the word yacht's is taken

parts.note: to moor a boat is to tie it up

explanation.surface: A roomy yacht is moored with its bow pointing north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading north' reverses YMOOR in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Spacious and its synonym both describe a place with plenty of room inside.

clue.text: Screen in position for start of show

parts.note: a curtain screens a window or stage
up can mean set in place, as shelves that are up

explanation.surface: A screen is set in its place ready for a performance to begin.
explanation.definitionFit: The theatrical phrase marks the moment the stage curtain rises and a performance begins.

clue.text: Friendly, am I? — Vince

parts.note: taken as written
Vince Cable is a British politician, once leader of the Liberal Democrats

explanation.surface: Someone asks Vince whether they are being friendly.
explanation.walkthrough: Vince Cable was a British Liberal Democrat leader and government minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Amicable is a synonym of friendly, describing relations that are cordial and peaceable.

clue.text: Separating from popular duo usually testing

indicators.note: the run of letters is separated out from the words that follow, which conceal it

explanation.surface: Breaking up from a popular double act is usually a trying experience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Separating from' signals the run hidden in popuLAR DUO USually.
explanation.definitionFit: Testing here means demanding or hard to bear, which is what an arduous task is.

clue.text: One uses strange material for debate

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: the letters of uses are made strange by being rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone uses odd material in their argument.
explanation.definitionFit: An issue is a topic or point in dispute, the stuff a debate is about.

clue.text: Continental's day in a prison

definitions.note: a native of a continent, with 's read as is

indicators.note: the day's abbreviation is placed in the middle of the other two pieces

parts.note: can is slang for prison
Fri is the abbreviation for Friday

explanation.surface: A European spends a day in a prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Continental' usually means European, but here it is someone from another continent.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Africa is a native of that continent, so a continental in the literal sense.

clue.text: Has this ever been seen as a Scottish tourist attraction?

definitions.text: Has this ever been seen as a Scottish tourist attraction?

parts.words: Has this ever been seen as a Scottish tourist attraction?
parts.note: the joke is that the creature draws visitors yet has never been reliably sighted

explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks whether something is regarded as an attraction; the cryptic sense asks whether it has ever actually been seen.
explanation.definitionFit: The fabled creature of a Highland lake draws tourists to Scotland although sightings remain unproven.

clue.text: Hated a British host on air

indicators.note: spoken on air, as in broadcasting, signals a word given by its sound

parts.note: a host is a great crowd, a horde

explanation.surface: A British television host became widely disliked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on air' says HORDE is heard, giving HORRED.
explanation.definitionFit: Abhorred is the past form of abhor, to loathe, so it means detested.

clue.text: Walked out from small wagon

parts.note: a truck is a wagon

explanation.surface: Someone stepped down out of a little wagon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Walked out' looks like a stroll; it means went on strike.
explanation.definitionFit: Workers who struck went on strike, that is, they walked out of their jobs.

clue.text: Heartless description of cat causes anger

indicators.note: the middle letter, the heart of the word, is removed

parts.note: a cat may be described as furry

explanation.surface: A cruel way of describing a cat makes someone cross.
explanation.definitionFit: Fury is extreme anger, rage.

clue.text: Coming into a little money benefits youngster

indicators.note: the benefits go into the middle of the other piece

parts.note: a cent is a small coin
doles are welfare payments, benefits

explanation.surface: A young person comes into a small amount of money from welfare.
explanation.definitionFit: An adolescent is a teenager, a young person between child and adult.

clue.text: Start of play about fighting

parts.note: the first act of a play is Act I
on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A drama opens with a battle scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers in action are engaged in combat, so the noun covers fighting.

clue.text: At Mass, in perverted rite?

indicators.note: perverted means twisted out of shape, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A twisted ritual is held at a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: a perverted rite at Mass describes devil worship.
explanation.definitionFit: Devil worship often parodies the Christian Mass in a black mass, a perverted rite.

clue.text: Revolver found at entrance to ground

definitions.text: Revolver found at entrance to ground

parts.words: Revolver found at entrance to ground
parts.note: a revolver here is something that revolves, not a gun, at the gate of a sports ground

explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolver' suggests a pistol; it is a rotating gate.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotating barrier admits spectators one at a time at the gate of a stadium.

clue.text: At start of book, one gets stuck

definitions.text: At start of book, one gets stuck

parts.words: At start of book, one gets stuck
parts.note: not a reader stalling early on, but a leaf glued inside the cover

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a reader giving up on page one; the sheet is literally pasted down.
explanation.definitionFit: This leaf is pasted to the inside of a book's cover, at its front or back.

clue.text: Capered, like a follower of Rudolph?

definitions.meaning: Prancer is one of Santa's reindeer, following Rudolph, so this is acting the way that reindeer is named

explanation.surface: Someone frolicked about like one of Santa's reindeer.
explanation.definitionFit: To caper and its synonym both mean to leap and bound in high spirits.

clue.text: Complaint from the bar

definitions.meaning: a barrier of rails or a single rail, as in a fence

explanation.surface: A grumble is heard from the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the bar' suggests a pub; it is a fence rail.
explanation.definitionFit: To rail is to protest bitterly, and a railing is also a fence made of bars.

clue.text: Get back to CV

definitions.meaning: to take up again after a break
an account of one's career, used chiefly in American English for this sense

explanation.surface: Someone returns to working on their curriculum vitae.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to restart something, and the noun with an accent is a summary of a career.

clue.text: I hadn't changed teacher at random

indicators.note: the letters of the words are changed into a new order

parts.note: pupils address a female teacher as Miss

explanation.surface: Someone protests that they did not swap teachers.
explanation.definitionFit: Something haphazard succeeds by chance or fails, without any plan, so random.

clue.text: Some bandit took the same again

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A robber helped himself to another identical item.
explanation.definitionFit: Ditto marks or the word itself indicate a repeat of what was said before.

clue.text: Manage fine conclusion

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils
an end is a conclusion

explanation.surface: Someone is coping with a satisfactory finish.
explanation.definitionFit: To fend for oneself is to cope or get by without help.

clue.text: Following cut, one dressed unattractively

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
rump is a cut of beef

explanation.surface: After a haircut, someone looks unfashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: A dowdy woman in drab, old-fashioned clothes is the classic image this word names.

clue.text: It supplies Americans with water

parts.note: the American word for what Britons call a tap

explanation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like a utility company; it is the device on a sink.
explanation.definitionFit: In the United States a tap on a sink or bath is called by this name.

clue.text: Announce resignation in city, after one evil act

indicators.note: the rest comes after the numeral one

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: the announcement goes inside the city's abbreviation

parts.note: NY is New York city
someone resigning announces I quit

explanation.surface: A wicked deed follows someone quitting their job in a city.
explanation.definitionFit: An iniquity is a grossly unjust or wicked act, a sin.

clue.text: Leader has ache, at full speed

parts.note: a head is a leader
to long for is to ache for

explanation.surface: The boss is suffering pain while racing along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ache' looks like a noun but is the verb to yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: Rushing headlong is moving recklessly fast, at top speed.

clue.text: I leave the country to earn money

definitions.text: I leave the country to earn money

parts.words: I leave the country to earn money
parts.note: the speaker is not an emigrant worker but goods sent abroad for sale

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as an emigrant worker speaking; the speaker is a product sold abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods sold to foreign buyers leave the home nation and bring in revenue.
